frame: ICRS J2000 to the existing Galactic-axis adapter; Unity world (Galactic X,Z,Y)
spin_policy: Static observed-epoch snapshots; rotationPeriod=0, alignRotationToOrbit=false, spinAroundDiskAxis=true. No rigid-body rotation period or spiral phase is inferred.

galaxies.note: The existing plane is correct. Local bar angle 25 minus world yaw 55 gives a world XZ bar angle of -30 degrees, with its near end at positive Galactic longitude. A 30-degree long-bar angle is within the published 28-33-degree range. Spiral phase and detailed warp are estimates.

sources.reference: Wegg, Gerhard & Portail (2015), structure of the Milky Way long bar
sources.adoption: Choose 30 degrees for the long bar; preserve the Galactic XZ plane.

galaxies.note: Representative main stellar disk plane; outer warps and the near-side ambiguity are not resolved by this PA/inclination pair. Preserve the existing placement distance, but use the correct heliocentric sky direction and the Sun parent. The old 3e22-m SOI enclosed Sol; use a 100-pc game core boundary, matching the generator maximum, not a measured black-hole influence radius.

sources.reference: Zhang et al. (2024), rotation curve and mass distribution of M31, adopted geometry
sources.adoption: Use the adopted main disk geometry and center; retain the mod distance.

galaxies.note: Representative inner stellar disk plane, not the warped outer gas disk. PA uncertainty is about 2 degrees; tilt, near side, and spiral phase have additional modeling uncertainty. Preserve the existing placement distance.

sources.reference: Corbelli et al. (2019), Rise and fall of molecular clouds across the M33 disk
sources.adoption: Use the inner disk geometry; a single plane cannot reproduce the outer warp.

galaxies.note: The smooth envelope represents the resolved host, not the combined 64-pc point-source-plus-host size. The existing central accretion effect is retained separately; its brightness is not fitted to the observed nuclear flux. The uncertain northeastern haze is omitted. The published PA is adopted as the sky major-axis angle; true depth, detailed profile and infrared display colors are approximations.

envelope.profile: Gaussian approximation to resolved rest-UV host
envelope.size_policy: Preserve measured apparent angle at the comoving positioning distance; scaled-space factor 6000.
envelope.color_policy: Near-infrared/rest-UV light mapped to pale blue for display; not a visible-light or calibrated photometric prediction.
envelope.display_status: Estimated display exposure checked in an enlarged isolated Unity renderer preview; no absolute photometric calibration.

sources.reference: Tacchella et al. (2023), section 3.2 and Table 2

galaxies.note: Adopt the observed image-plane size and elongation, including any foreground lensing; do not de-lens them and then render at the unlensed angular size. ForcePho angle is north of east, converted to east of north as 90 - degrees(1.427). The smooth Gaussian approximates a measured near-exponential profile; true depth, detailed structure and infrared display colors are uncertain. No mature spiral arms or central black hole are inferred.

envelope.profile: Gaussian approximation to resolved rest-UV host
envelope.size_policy: Preserve measured apparent angle at the comoving positioning distance; scaled-space factor 6000.
envelope.color_policy: Near-infrared/rest-UV light mapped to pale blue for display; not a visible-light or calibrated photometric prediction.
envelope.display_status: Estimated display exposure checked in an enlarged isolated Unity renderer preview; no absolute photometric calibration.

sources.reference: ForcePho Source.pa documents north-of-east angles; slow/gaussmodel.py uses a standard counterclockwise rotation in (east,north).
sources.adoption: Convert the raw fitted PA to the east-of-north convention used by the orbit-to-world orientation adapter.
